thread:
tara.p: noticed a handful of production alerts where an API key with org-admin intent failed project-level enforcement and returned 403s. looked like workers normalized scope to project-only during RBAC lookup
diego.l: can you paste an example token envelope? is this only the legacy `scope` claim shape?
tara.p: minimal example: internal keys minted `scope=org:acme:admin` but some pooled workers canonicalize to `project:acme-main` when routing affinity is applied
ben.m: ugh, that's the old normalization bug. worker lookup does a canonicalize(scopes) step which loses the original namespace if key didn't carry explicit origin claim
nora.h: long-term we should stop relying on inference. short-term fix: attach a compact capability envelope header at the edge so downstream can pick the right policy graph node without guessing
diego.l: what do you mean by capability envelope?
nora.h: a tiny signed blob produced at the auth edge with: kid, origin_type (org|project|service), primary_scope, exp, and a hash pointer to the policy version. header `X-Cap-Env: base64(...)`
ben.m: header size + verify cost = concern. C++ hot-path verifies a single HMAC today. adding crypto could be painful for p95
tara.p: proposal: make envelope verification optional -> workers accept envelope and use it when present; otherwise fall back to current canonicalize path. envelope should be ed25519-signed with short TTL (5s) and a kid for cached pubkey lookup
ora.h: pseudocode idea:
```
cap = parse_base64(header["X-Cap-Env"])
if (cap && verify_cached_key(cap.kid, cap.sig)) {
  policy_node = fetch_policy(cap.policy_hash) || fallback_policy(cap.primary_scope)
} else {
  policy_node = canonicalize(scopes_from_token)
}
```
sec-bot: perf-check: add metric auth.envelope.verify_latency and auth.envelope.miss_rate
diego.l: we can optimize verify by caching kid->pubkey and by verifying only the first request per connection; also fast-path for allowlisted edge ips
ora.h: migration plan: 1) edge emits envelope for new keys only (no enforcement). 2) roll workers to consume with opt-in flag. 3) enable envelope-preference for RBAC lookup for specific routes. 4) require for org-scoped keys after 2 weeks stable metrics
ora.h: also need a revocation path for edge signing keys and a KMS rotation schedule
ben.m: RBAC side: we should add a canonicalizer that preserves origin tag on policy nodes. when envelope present, we consult origin-prefixed index: policy_index[origin_type][scope_hash] then fallback to policy_index[project][scope_hash]
tara.p: tests: add negative tests that deliberately route org-key to project-only worker and assert envelope resolves correctly
diego.l: ops: will create alert if auth.envelope.verify_latency > 1ms or if origin_mismatch_rate increases during canary
ora.h: security review: replay resistance -> include ts+nonce in envelope and enforce short TTL, also include route-id so envelope can't be reused across regions
ora.h: example envelope payload (before base64): {"kid":"edge-1","origin":"org","scope":"acme","ts":2766123456,"policy_hash":"sha256:abc"} signed
ben.m: implementation note: workers should not fetch full policy graph synchronously in verify path. fetch policy metadata (policy_hash -> node_id) and evaluate against cached policy shards
sec-bot: ticket ENGSEC-2150 created: capability-envelope-design + key-rotation-checklist
tara.p: action items:
- nora.h: write design doc + envelope spec (T+1d)
- ben.m: extend RBAC canonicalizer to honor origin_prefixed lookup (T+2d)
- diego.l: add canary alerts and metric instrumentation (T+1d)
- tara.p: coordinate canary and tests, roll plan (T+3d)
- ops-bot: create KMS rotation runbook and revocation endpoint (ENGSEC-2150)
diego.l: small follow-up: need to update SDKs that mint keys to optionally request envelope emission flag so edge knows which tokens to envelope
tara.p: good call. also update docs: when creating legacy keys include `compat: true` so edge still emits envelope for them during migration
ora.h: final thought: this makes RBAC decisions explicit and decouples runtime from brittle inference. careful with key ops though, mis-rotations could blow up auth surface
tara.p: agreed. we'll do staged rollout and keep a short rollback path
ben.m: i'll prototype canonicalizer change and a microbenchmark for envelope verify cost
sec-bot: reminder: add SLO change request if p95 auth latency changes by >5%
tara.p: thanks all. ping here when you push the first PRs and when canary runs
